data.command: Explain T1547.001 Registry Run Keys persistence

data.text:
webapp@web-srv-01:~$ man mitre-t1547.001

T1547.001  Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder (MITRE ATT&CK)

Persistence technique. Adversaries modify the Windows registry so that a
program executes automatically at user logon, without requiring the user to
launch it manually.

HOW IT WORKS
------------
Windows reads specific registry keys during user logon and launches every
executable listed under the "Run" value of those keys.

Primary keys monitored:

  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
      Per-user. Survives reboots, applies only to the current user.
  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
      Per-user, single execution, then removed.
  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
      All users, machine-wide. Requires write access to HKLM.
  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
      Machine-wide, single execution.
  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunServices
      Runs before the user logs on (service context).
  HKCU\...\Policies\Explorer\Run
      Legacy key, still honored on some builds.

The value is a REG_SZ string. Typical payload shape:

  "UpdateService" = "C:\Users\Public\.cache\svc.exe"
  "WinUpdate"     = "\"C:\Program Files\WinUpd\wupd.exe\" -hidden"

Companion persistence (same TTP, different location):
  %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup
  %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup
  %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup

DETECTION SIGNALS
-----------------
  - New value written under any of the Run keys.
  - RegKey/RegValue audit events (Event ID 4657 / 4658, 12345).
  - Sysmon Event ID 13 with TargetObject matching the Run path.
  - Executable path outside normal install dirs (Public, Temp, Temp
    folders, AppData, ProgramData, or a hidden dot-folder).
  - Quoted-path trickery or cmd.exe /c wrapper to evade simple string
    matching.
  - Value name mimicking legitimate software to blend in.

DEFENSE / MITIGATION
--------------------
  - Restrict write access to HKLM Run keys via ACLs.
  - AppLocker / WDAC to block execution from user-writable paths.
  - Enable audit policy for registry changes on the Run keys.
  - Sysmon config: audit RegValueSet on the Run key paths.
  - EDR baseline of known-good Run entries; alert on delta.
  - Prefer logon scripts / GPO / scheduled tasks with proper ownership
    over user-writable Run keys for legitimate autostart needs.

CROSS-REFERENCES
-----------------
  T1547.002  Scheduled Task/Job (alternative autostart)
  T1547.004  Winlogon Helper DLL
  T1547.006  Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription
  T1547.009  Shortcut Modification
